related_questions.question: What disease is caused by Balantidium coli?
related_questions.snippet: Overview. Balantidium coli is an intestinal protozoan parasite that causes the infection called balantidiasis. While this type of infection is uncommon in the United States, humans and other mammals can become infected with Balantidium coli by ingesting infective cysts from food and water that is contaminated by feces.

related_questions.question: What diseases are caused by E coli?

text_blocks.snippet: E. coli bacteria can cause a range of illnesses, from mild diarrhea to severe and life-threatening conditions. Common infections include urinary tract infections (UTIs), gastroenteritis (often with diarrhea), and, in severe cases, hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS), which can lead to kidney failure.
snippet_highlighted_words: urinary tract infections (UTIs), gastroenteritis (often with diarrhea), and, in severe cases, hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS), which can lead to kidney failure

list.title: Diarrhea:
list.snippet: E. coli can cause watery, bloody, or inflammatory diarrhea, often accompanied by abdominal cramps and vomiting.

list.title: Hemorrhagic Colitis:
list.snippet: Certain strains of E. coli, particularly E. coli O157:H7, produce toxins that damage the lining of the small intestine, leading to bloody diarrhea.

list.title: Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS):
list.snippet: A serious complication of E. coli infection, especially with E. coli O157:H7, HUS can cause kidney failure, anemia, and low platelet count.

list.title: Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs):
list.snippet: E. coli is a common cause of UTIs, including cystitis (bladder infection) and pyelonephritis (kidney infection).

list.title: Other Infections:
list.snippet: E. coli can also cause pneumonia, bacteremia (bloodstream infection), meningitis (especially in newborns), and infections in other areas like the gallbladder, peritoneum, skin, and lungs.

list.title: Sepsis:
list.snippet: In severe cases, E. coli bloodstream infections can lead to sepsis, a life-threatening condition.
Children under 5: Young children are more susceptible to severe E. coli infections and HUS.
Adults 65 and older: Older adults also have an increased risk of complications.
People with weakened immune systems: Individuals with compromised immune systems are more vulnerable.
International travelers: Travelers may encounter different strains of E. coli in other countries.
Proper food handling and cooking: Thoroughly cook ground beef and other meats, wash fruits and vegetables, and avoid unpasteurized dairy products.
Safe water practices: Drink treated or bottled water, especially when traveling.
Hygiene: Wash hands frequently, especially after using the restroom and before preparing food.

text_blocks.snippet: Balantidiasis is a rare intestinal infection caused by the parasite Balantidium coli, primarily affecting humans through fecal-oral transmission from pigs. While many infections are asymptomatic, symptomatic cases can manifest as diarrhea, abdominal pain, and in severe cases, dysentery, colitis, or even extraintestinal complications.
snippet_highlighted_words: Balantidiasis is a rare intestinal infection caused by the parasite Balantidium coli, primarily affecting humans through fecal-oral transmission from pigs

text_blocks.snippet: Key aspects of Balantidium coli infection:

list.title: Causative Agent:
list.snippet: Balantidium coli is a ciliated protozoan parasite, the largest of its kind to infect humans.

list.title: Transmission:
list.snippet: Infection occurs through ingestion of cysts from contaminated food or water, often from pigs, which are a common reservoir.

list.title: Prevalence:
list.snippet: While found worldwide, it is more common in tropical and subtropical regions, especially where pig farming is prevalent and hygiene is poor.
Asymptomatic: Many individuals have no noticeable symptoms.
Symptomatic: Symptoms can range from mild diarrhea and abdominal discomfort to severe, bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, and even dysentery or colitis.
Severe Cases: Immunocompromised individuals are at higher risk for severe disease, potentially including extraintestinal complications like peritonitis or liver abscesses.

list.title: Diagnosis:
list.snippet: Microscopic examination of stool samples showing Balantidium coli trophozoites or cysts is the primary method of diagnosis, according to LabCE.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Metronidazole is the drug of choice for treating balantidiasis.

list.title: Prevention:
list.snippet: Maintaining good hygiene practices, including proper handwashing after using the toilet and before handling food, and ensuring safe drinking water are crucial for preventing infection, according to the CDC.
